messages:

Subject: QBR capacity & unit-econ runbook — scenario deconflicters

Team —

As we pull the QBR packet together, I want to align on a compact runbook that surfaces the hard tradeoffs between reserved capacity, burst slots, and KV/batching levers for the Exec presentation. High-level ask: please review the attached workbook (QBR_scenarios_v3.xlsx) and the appendix on batching/KV cache impact. I need a short, prioritized list of the three scenarios we want leadership to approve for runway hedging.

Things to consider (brief):
- GPU spend delta: baseline reserved + autoscale vs. burst-enabled (example numbers in sheet show ~24% higher monthly commitment for the conservative reserved plan).
- Utilization assumptions: baseline 55% average slot utilization; improved batching/KV cache can push effective utilization to 68% for text-gen workloads with 90-token med seq.
- Unit economics: per-k token cost sensitivity tied to batching depth (sheet tab "batch-sensitivity") — small gain in batch size yields nonlinear cost wins for long-tail traffic.
- SLAs & fallbacks: can we show a fallback chain (hosted -> dedicated -> smaller model) with expected latency/Q loss?

Specific asks by Thursday EOD:
1) Lauren: one-slide summary for Exec with the three scenarios and the single-number ask for each (commit $ / expected unit-cost improvement / risk).
2) Karthik: validate the utilization model inputs and sanity-check the 68% uplift numbers — note in the workbook where you tweak assumptions.
3) Marissa: confirm whether our current marketplace discounts (Nimbus Cloud) can be modeled as a deferred credit vs. reduced commit — this materially impacts the preferred scenario.
4) Dylan: quick call with Nimbus ops to confirm burst slot availability (I list them in CC to start the thread).

Attach: QBR_scenarios_v3.xlsx, batch-cache-impact-appendix.pdf (both in Drive link).

I want the slide bullets by Friday COB so we can iterate with Comms on Saturday.

Thanks —

Tessa Morgan
Head of Ops Strategy
Redwood Inference

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-06T12:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR capacity & unit-econ runbook — scenario deconflicters

Tessa —

Thanks. I pulled the sheet into the Exec slide template and sketched three scenarios (overview pasted below). I kept the ask numbers deliberately tight so they map to quota/commit brackets we already discuss with Finance.

Scenario A — Conservative reserve
- Commit: $1.2M/mo reserved (covers 70% of baseline traffic)
- Expected avg slot util: 57%
- Unit-cost improvement: +8% vs current monthly spend (mainly from reserved discounts)
- Risk: high upfront commit; lower headroom for spikes

Scenario B — Hybrid + aggressive cache/batching optimization
- Commit: $850k/mo reserved + burst pool policy (on-demand)
- Expected avg slot util: 66% after KV cache + batching tuning (see tab "opt-paths")
- Unit-cost improvement: +18% (mix of reserved discount and efficiency gains)
- Risk: operational complexity; needs a 3-week ops sprint to hit caching thresholds

Scenario C — Minimal reserve + model variant routing
- Commit: $450k/mo reserved; heavier use of smaller quantized variants for tail
- Expected avg slot util: 60% effective unit-cost improvement: +12% (also reduces cold-start cost)
- Risk: slightly lower quality for a fraction of requests; requires routing heatmap

Notes: I flagged the math cells where a 5% change in utilization flips the preferred scenario (sheet tab 'sensitivity_bracket'). Karthik — I left comments where assumptions look thin (seq length distribution and production batch depth).

Next steps: I can convert the above into a single slide with a 1-line recommendation if you want me to take a first pass.

— Lauren
VP, Infrastructure Planning
Redwood Inference

Quick notes from Procurement angle —

- Nimbus is willing to structure the discount two ways: a flat 12% off list for a 12-month commit, or a $200k deferred credit applied after quarter-end if we take a smaller commit this quarter but demonstrate utilization targets. The former reduces reported monthly unit cost immediately; the latter helps runway but is more contingent.
- EdgeMetrics (vendor handling slot telemetry) confirmed we can enable per-customer KV-cache heatmaps; that helps prove the 66% utilization target if we run a 3-week cache pilot.
- Attachment: I pasted summary rows into the workbook (tab 'procurement_notes').

Recommend we show Exec the Hybrid (Scenario B) as our preferred ask with clear contingency: if Nimbus doesn't accept the hybrid pricing (deferred credit), we pivot to Scenario A. That keeps the ask binary and easy to approve.

Marissa Cole
Head of Procurement
Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, dylan_brooks@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-08T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: QBR capacity & unit-econ runbook — scenario deconflicters

All —

I validated the utilization model and ran a sensitivity sweep (attached changes in QBR_scenarios_v3.xlsx; I added a tab 'sensitivity_run' with Monte Carlo draws). Summary:

- The 68% uplift number is attainable but rests on two conditions: (1) median batch depth increases from 3.2 -> 5.1 for long-tail traffic and (2) KV cache hit-rate >= 47% on repeat prefixes. If either falls short by >6pp, the cost advantage shrinks to single-digit improvements.
- Latency impact: projected p95 increases by ~40–60ms under deeper batching for some interactive paths; recommend we keep a 15% traffic slice on low-latency routing to avoid customer-visible regressions.
- Burst availability: Dylan and I confirmed with Nimbus that a 200-slot burst pool is provisionable in our preferred region with a 6–12 hour lead time for scale-up. That dovetails with Marissa's deferred-credit option.

Recommendation (for Exec slide):
1) Ask: Approve Scenario B (Hybrid + optimization) with a fallback to Scenario A if procurement cannot secure deferred credit.
2) Ops guardrails: reserve a 15% low-latency routing band, run a 3-week cache pilot in Week 1 of the quarter, and commit to a two-sprint optimization plan (4 weeks) before re-evaluating unit economics.

I'll finalize the one-paragraph justification and the key metrics cell for the slide deck by tomorrow morning.

Karthik Iyer
Director, Performance Modeling
Redwood Inference
